property_summary: Only calls to withdraw initiated by the contract Owner succeed (do not revert) — calls from non-Owner revert.
withdraw only succeeds when caller equals the contract's Owner (i.e., the call to withdraw reverts iff caller != c.Owner()).
The withdraw call reverts exactly when the provided caller address is not equal to c.Owner().
The withdraw call reverts iff the provided caller address is not equal to c.Owner().

For all callers and inputs, calling Command(addr,data) must not change the effect of withdraw: in the correct contract only Owner can withdraw the contract balance (so after a non-owner calls Command the contract balance can only be withdrawn by Owner), whereas the mutant removing the require in withdraw allows anyone to invoke withdraw (via Command) and steal the balance; thus the reference preserves that withdraw succeeds only when invoked by Owner while the mutant allows non-owners to cause balance transfer to Owner via Command for some inputs.

For any caller and calldata, only the contract Owner can cause the contract balance to be transferred out via withdraw (i.e., withdraw succeeds only when called by Owner); the mutant removing the require allows a non-Owner to trigger a transfer of the contract balance through Command -> withdraw interaction for some inputs, violating this invariant.

Invariant: Only Owner can cause the contract to transfer out its balance when invoking withdraw() — after any call to Command(address,bytes) by any caller (with any calldata and value), a subsequent direct call to withdraw() by a non-Owner must NOT succeed in reducing address(c).balance in the reference, but the mutant (which removed the require in withdraw) allows some non-Owner to cause the balance to be sent to Owner and thus reduce address(c).balance.

For all callers and calldata, calling Command on an adversarial contract that reverts its fallback must not allow a non-Owner caller to cause the c contract's balance to be forwarded out by withdraw (i.e., after such Command, only Owner can successfully withdraw the balance) — the mutant (which removes the require in withdraw) allows a non-Owner actor to make withdraw transfer the balance out, violating this rule.

For every caller and calldata,value the correct contract C ensures that only Owner can successfully transfer out the contract balance via withdraw() (so address(c).balance remains unchanged after a non-Owner attempts withdraw), whereas the mutant that removes the require allows some non-Owner to cause the contract balance to be transferred out (address(c).balance decreases) for some inputs.
Only the Owner address can successfully call withdraw() to transfer the contract balance to Owner.
Calls to withdraw revert for any caller that is not the contract's stored Owner, so a non-Owner caller cannot successfully complete withdraw.

For every caller and Ether amount, calling withdraw transfers the contract balance to the stored Owner (so address(c).balance becomes 0 and Owner's balance increases accordingly); the mutant that transfers to msg.sender instead can send funds to the caller, violating that Owner must be the recipient for some inputs.

For any caller and any contract balance, after Owner (the stored Owner) calls withdraw(), the contract balance becomes 0 and Owner (the stored Owner) receives the funds; the mutant that sends funds to msg.sender instead will for some caller cause the stored Owner to not receive the funds (i.e., Owner's balance does not increase as expected).

For any caller and any contract balance funded via payable calls, when the stored Owner calls withdraw(), the contract balance becomes zero and the Owner's address is the recipient of the funds (i.e., address(c).balance == 0 after Owner withdraws); the mutant that sends to msg.sender can break this by sending funds to a different address when Owner is the caller, so we assert that after Owner calls withdraw() the contract balance is zero (which the mutant can violate by transferring elsewhere before balance becomes zero in observable way).

When the stored Owner calls withdraw(), the funds MUST be sent to Owner (so Owner's balance increases by the contract balance and address(c).balance becomes zero); the mutant that sends to msg.sender can redirect funds away from the stored Owner when Owner != msg.sender (i.e., when the stored Owner is an address that behaves adversarially), so the rule is violated for some inputs.

For any caller who is the stored Owner and any initial contract balance, when Owner calls withdraw() the contract's balance becomes zero afterwards (the reference always empties the contract to Owner); the mutant that transfers to msg.sender can cause the contract to retain a non-zero balance for some inputs (when the low-level transfer to Owner fails), thus violating this rule.

For any caller who is Owner, calling withdraw transfers the entire contract balance to Owner (so address(c).balance becomes 0); the mutant that transfers 0 breaks this by leaving a nonzero contract balance for some inputs.

For any caller that is the Owner and when the contract holds a positive balance, calling withdraw() empties the contract balance (address(c).balance == 0) in the reference; the mutant that transfers 0 breaks this by leaving a nonzero balance for some inputs.

For any caller who is the Owner and when the contract has a positive balance, calling withdraw() always results in address(c).balance == 0 in the reference; the mutant that replaces the transfer amount with 0 can leave address(c).balance > 0 for some inputs (Owner with positive balance).

For any owner caller and any positive contract balance funded by sending ether to multiplicate() with msg.value >= address(c).balance, calling withdraw() will result in address(c).balance == 0 (reference does transfer full balance); the mutant that changes transfer to send 0 breaks this by leaving a nonzero contract balance for some inputs.

For any Owner caller and any pre-funded contract balance > 0, calling withdraw() empties the contract (address(c).balance == 0); the mutant that transfers 0 breaks this by leaving a nonzero contract balance for some inputs.

Reference contract always reverts and does not forward control when Owner's fallback reverts (withdraw either succeeds without calling into a malicious fallback because transfer forwards limited gas and reverts on failure), whereas the mutant using call will propagate/observe the callee's behavior (succeed/fail) allowing a malicious Owner fallback to change the outcome; thus the property: withdraw never succeeds when Owner's fallback reverts in the reference, but the mutant can behave differently for some inputs.

If Owner's fallback reverts when called, then the reference contract's withdraw() always reverts (transfer bubbles revert), while the mutant using call may succeed for some input/actor setups; we deploy a reverter Owner and fuzz the initial funding amount to find a case where the mutant would behave differently.

For every caller and funding amount, when Owner's fallback uses only limited gas (no reentrancy) the reference contract's withdraw always transfers the full contract balance atomically (so address(c).balance == 0 after withdraw), whereas the mutant using call can fail to zero the balance for some setups where the external call behaviour or gas semantics differ.

For any owner address whose fallback consumes all gas by reverting, the reference contract's withdraw() ALWAYS reverts (so the call does not succeed), while the mutant that uses low-level call may return a different success value for some fuzzed funding amounts and attacker setups; we assert that withdraw reverts (ok == false) for all admissible inputs.

For any owner address whose fallback reverts, the reference contract's withdraw() always reverts (so a withdraw call by the owner cannot succeed if the owner's fallback reverts), while the mutant using call can return success for some fuzzed funding amounts and thus may not revert — so we assert that withdraw always reverts when owner fallback reverts.
Calling Command with a nonzero msg.value forwards the call (does not revert) so the external call succeeds and does not revert.
Calling Command with msg.sender == Owner never reverts (succeeds) even if the target call fails, so the call/transfer failure does not make Command revert.

For any callee address that reverts when receiving value, the reference forwards msg.value in Command so the external call reverts (or behaves differently) while the mutant that drops value makes the call succeed; hence for all inputs the reference ensures a failing-value-forwarding call does not succeed, which the mutant can break for some inputs by omitting value forwarding.

For any caller and any value, if the caller sends Ether when invoking Command to forward that value to a callee that always reverts on payable calls, the reference C always observes the external call to revert (because it forwards msg.value), while the mutant that drops value can make the external call succeed for some fuzzed value and callee (thus differing observable behavior); we assert that calling Command on c with a payable-reverting callee and sending a fuzzed amount always causes the call to revert for the reference.

For any caller and any amount, when Owner calls Command forwarding msg.value to a callee contract that REVERTs when receiving value, the reference C always observes the external call to revert (the call fails), whereas the mutant that drops value can make the external call succeed for some fuzzed amount by not forwarding msg.value.

For any caller (Owner) and any amount, when Command is invoked sending msg.value to a callee whose fallback/receive requires msg.value to be zero (i.e. it reverts if value>0), the reference C always causes the external call to revert (so Command call fails); the mutant that drops value can make Command succeed for some inputs by not forwarding msg.value.

For any caller Owner and any ether amount, when Command is invoked with the Owner sending value to an external callee whose fallback always reverts on non-zero value, the reference C always causes Command to revert (because it forwards msg.value) while the mutant that drops value can make Command succeed for some fuzzed amount by not forwarding value.
